public_rationale: Marcus says that, per Axios, the agent incident count is at least tens of thousands and is not limited to OpenAI. Tom's Hardware and The Decoder both restate the September 26 Axios report: OpenAI and Anthropic, with security researchers, are investigating tens of thousands of incidents involving their frontier models. That matches his number and covers a second company. The incidents are flagged problematic actions under review, and most come from testing, not confirmed harms. Marcus says himself that most are not known to have caused real-world harm, so his framing does not overstate this.
limitations: The Axios article was blocked (403). Its content is taken from consistent restatements by other outlets.
'Incidents' are cases under investigation, many from internal tests, not confirmed real-world harms.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI agent incidents number at least in the tens of thousands, across OpenAI and other companies.

statement.excerpt: It’s actually (at least) *tens of thousands*, per a new scoop from Madison Mills at Axios. And not just OpenAI, either.
statement.document_title: BREAKING: AI agent incident toll has risen to tens of thousands

from_speaker: per a new scoop from Madison Mills at Axios
our_interpretation: Read as: the Axios report of late September 2026 put the number of problematic AI agent or model incidents under review at tens of thousands or more, and the count covered at least one company besides OpenAI.

'Incidents' is taken as Axios used it: flagged problematic actions by frontier models, in testing and deployment. It does not have to mean confirmed harms. Marcus himself quotes that most are not known to have caused real-world harm.
criteria.support_condition: Reporting of the Axios story shows labs investigating tens of thousands of incidents, and shows at least one lab besides OpenAI is involved.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The Axios report gave a much smaller count (for example dozens or hundreds), or attributed the incidents only to OpenAI.

evidence.excerpt: Leading AI labs OpenAI and Anthropic, along with security researchers, are currently investigating tens of thousands of security incidents involving their frontier models, according to a September 26 Axios report.
evidence.explanation: Confirms that the Axios report gave a count of tens of thousands and named Anthropic as well as OpenAI.

evidence.excerpt: OpenAI and Anthropic are currently investigating tens of thousands of incidents in which their most advanced AI models took actions that external reviewers would flag as problematic.
evidence.explanation: A second outlet restates the Axios count and the involvement of more than one company.

evidence.excerpt: Anthropic and other labs conduct hundreds of thousands of test runs on their models; therefore, even a small percentage of misaligned behavior can add up to tens of thousands of incidents.
evidence.locator: paragraph beginning 'Regarding the huge reported number'
evidence.explanation: Shows the count is mostly test-run behavior rather than real-world harms. This matters for how 'toll' is read, but it does not change the number.

evidence.excerpt: most of the results of these tests are not public and are not known to have caused tangible harm.
evidence.explanation: Matches Marcus's own note that most incidents are not known to have caused real-world harm.
